\section[il testamento]{il testamento — the will, the testament}

\label{lesson:IT-C314-testamento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for mourning, then the Italian for to bury.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il testamento}
\textbf{il testamento} — \textquotedblleft{}the will, the testament\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il nonno ha lasciato un testamento.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Grandfather left a will.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fare testamento} — to make a will.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{testamento} is inherited from Latin \emph{testāmentum} \textquotedblleft{}a will\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{testārī} \textquotedblleft{}to bear witness\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il testamento}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il testamento}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il testamento}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for mourning, then the Italian for to bury, then say \emph{il testamento} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does il testamento mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The will, the testament\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ereditare]{ereditare — to inherit}

\label{lesson:IT-C314-ereditare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to bury, then the Italian for the will.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: ereditare}
\textbf{ereditare} — \textquotedblleft{}to inherit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ho ereditato la casa di mia zia.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I inherited my aunt's house.}
\end{quote}

Also for looks: \emph{ha ereditato gli occhi del padre}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ereditare} is inherited from Late Latin \emph{hērēditāre} (EtymDB), built on \emph{hērēs} \textquotedblleft{}heir\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[l'eredità]{l'eredità — the inheritance; heritage}

Before the new one: say the Italian for the will, then the Italian for to inherit.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'eredità}

\section[l'erede]{l'erede — the heir}

\label{lesson:IT-C314-erede}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to inherit, then the Italian for the inheritance.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'erede}

\end{quote}

One form for a man or a woman.

\emph{erede} is inherited from Latin \emph{hērēs} \textquotedblleft{}heir, heiress\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).

\section[la tomba]{la tomba — the grave, the tomb}

\label{lesson:IT-C314-tomba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the inheritance, then the Italian for the heir.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la tomba}
\textbf{la tomba} — \textquotedblleft{}the grave, the tomb\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ogni anno portiamo fiori sulla tomba dei nonni.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Every year we take flowers to our grandparents' grave.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Muto come una tomba} — silent as the grave.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tomba} is inherited from Late Latin \emph{tumba} (EtymDB), from Greek \emph{týmbos} \textquotedblleft{}a burial mound\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
